title: row05
live_proof: the defect is public and fixed upstream in 3.29.0, after the 3.22.0 pin; sqlite3_blob_close() in the pinned tree uses the lookaside-allocated Incrblob with no guard against the connection having been closed
object: the Incrblob, allocated from the connection's lookaside pool
lifetime_ender: sqlite3_close_v2() frees the connection and its lookaside pool while the blob handle is still open
fidelity: real consumer, real allocator: SQLite's own memsys5 heap with lookaside on. This case predates the group harness and still talks to the older hostcall interface, which is why the Sublet arm skips it -- the standalone domain has no Sublet grant glue for it

sublet.oracle: fault at cause 24, untagged dereference, pc=0x800239e4 -- detected (2026-10-05). Runnable at all only after the case was ported from the legacy standalone domain onto REPRO322_MAIN: the old entry point never captured the Sublet grant, so memsys5Init faulted before the case ran.

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: CheriBSD 15.0-CURRENT riscv64-purecap, memsys5 over the case's static arena (shared/run-cheribsd.py --mode nested). Revocation acts on a guest malloc free, and under memsys5 there is none: sqlite3_free returns the block to memsys5's own pool inside one array the guest allocator sees as a single live object. So a tag fault here is NOT revocation reporting -- SIGPROT(34) with si_code=2 at the function host ASan reported (fault_sites) is recorded as a catch by the same rule the virtual arms use, and the note says what actually cleared the tag. A fault anywhere else is not tied to the defect
cheribsd-revocation.verdict_note: the case RETURNED (exit 0) and this arm reported nothing; the run's poscontrol gate FAULTed (exit=162, revocation_default=1) before any case ran

status: all three arms run; spatial and sublet 2026-10-04 with the gaps closed 2026-10-05, cheribsd-revocation 2026-10-04 with the 12 missing cases built and run 2026-10-05
fault_sites_why: sqlite3_blob_close frees the lookaside-allocated Incrblob through sqlite3DbFree after sqlite3_close_v2 freed the connection and its lookaside pool, so the stale reads are sqlite3DbFreeNN's (consumer; PROVENANCE.md). Declared 2026-10-10 after the virtual runs resolved faults there; the reason is the source and PROVENANCE.md cited, which predate those runs.
